title: Effects of a 4-Week Supplementation with a Multi-Nutrient Combination on Coenzyme Q10 Status
summary:
Many people do not obtain adequate amounts of all essential vitamins and minerals. Multinutrient supplements may help improve the intake of these nutrients. However, little is currently known about the effects of combined supplementation with different nutrients on health.
One component of the supplement under investigation, BIOGENA ONE, is coenzyme Q10, which plays an important role in cellular energy production. Studies suggest that coenzyme Q10 may have beneficial effects on blood pressure. Potential effects on fatigue and sleep quality are also being discussed.
This study aims to investigate whether four weeks of supplementation with BIOGENA ONE leads to changes in coenzyme Q10 status, blood pressure, and subjective sleep quality.
conditions: Suboptimal micronutrient status and associated impairments in energy levels, fatigue, sleep quality, and subjective well-being in otherwise healthy adults.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Body mass index (BMI) ≥ 25 kg/m²
Written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
Missing informed consent
Current participation in another interventional study
Pregnancy or breastfeeding
Smoking
Excessive physical activity (≥ 10 hours per week)
Wilson’s disease
Acute or chronic infections (e.g., HIV, hepatitis B virus, hepatitis C virus, tuberculosis)
Untreated hyperthyroidism or hypothyroidism
Untreated hypertension (> 160/95 mmHg)
Treatment with vitamin K antagonists (e.g., phenprocoumon or warfarin)
Regular long-term use of anti-inflammatory medications
Implanted pacemaker
Cancer within the past 6 months or radiochemotherapy within the past 3 years
Chronic gastrointestinal diseases (e.g., inflammatory bowel disease, coeliac disease)
Known diabetes mellitus (type 1 or type 2), or newly identified evidence of diabetes mellitus requiring treatment at screening, according to the criteria of the German Diabetes Association (DDG) or the World Health Organization (WHO), i.e., HbA1c ≥ 6.5% (48 mmol/mol) or fasting plasma glucose ≥ 126 mg/dL (7.0 mmol/L)
Known hypercalcaemia or elevated serum calcium levels above the laboratory-specific reference range at screening
Acute gastrointestinal conditions (e.g., diarrhoea) or bleeding disorders
Antibiotic use within 2 months prior to study enrolment
Planned surgery during the intervention period
Allergy to celery
Regular use of multinutrient supplements
